terrainNotes: Elevation data at this point, finest first: LOLA LDEM_60S_60M, 60 m site window (60 m per sample, to about 3.8 km); LOLA LDEM_60S_60M, 480 m site window (480 m per sample, to about 31 km); LOLA whole-Moon grid, 16 px/deg (1.9 km per sample, whole Moon).
Beyond about 31 km from the site only the whole-Moon grid is available (1.9 km per sample), which smooths ridges narrower than that; distant skyline peaks can read slightly low.

Where one grid hands over to the next, the heights do not match exactly. Around this site the outer grid differs from the inner one by: -21.2 to +22.7 m (6.6 m RMS) at 3.8 km, where the 60 m window ends; -221 to +127 m (52.4 m RMS) at 31 km, where the 480 m window ends. assumptions: Observer 2 m above the terrain at -69.3741, 32.3200 (degrees, east-positive, ME frame); heights above the 1737.4 km sphere.

Sampled every 5 min; rise and set times refined to 10 s; the Sun and Earth are discs (visible fraction integrated across each disc).
Sunrise/sunset = first/last moment any part of the Sun stands above the skyline. Earthrise/Earthset = Earth's centre crossing the skyline.

Earth visibility is geometric line of sight only; it says nothing about a working radio link.

station.name: Madrid DSS-63 (70 m)
station.complex: Robledo de Chavela, near Madrid, Spain

assumptions: Geometry only: an opportunity is an unobstructed straight line between the station and the site, with the site above the station's elevation limit and the station above the site's terrain skyline. It is not a statement about a working radio link: no link budget, frequency, antenna pattern, antenna scheduling or availability is considered.

Stations: the 70 m antennas DSS-14 (Goldstone), DSS-43 (Canberra) and DSS-63 (Madrid). Coordinates from the DSN Telecommunications Link Design Handbook, 810-005, Module 301 Rev. N (15 April 2022), Tables 2 and 5 (ITRF93 epoch 2003.0; WGS 84).

Elevation limits: 6.0 deg for receiving (the handbook's generic receive limit; the antennas' mechanical limit is about 6 deg) and, for transmitting, 10.4 deg at DSS-14 and 10.2 deg at DSS-43 and DSS-63 (the limits of the handbook's 70 m transmit coverage chart). The stations' own azimuth-dependent horizon masks are not applied: for instance the handbook keeps DSS-63 above 20.2 deg towards high ground to its north-west when transmitting, and high-power transmitters have higher limits.
At the site the direction to the station itself is tested against the skyline (the stations are up to 0.95 deg from the centre of Earth's disc).

Positions are geometric and airless (no tropospheric refraction); Earth's rotation uses UT1 = UTC without polar motion. Checked against JPL Horizons, the site as seen from each station: elevation within 0.0013 deg over 1154 instants (1971, 2025, 2034) and rise and set times through the limits within 0.3 s on the day compared; UT1 - UTC, at most 0.9 s, is the limit in general.
